RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the December 15, 2008/Agrahayana 24, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Food Processing Industries; Human Resource Development; Law
and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs; New and Renewable Energy; Power;
Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Women and Child
Development)
Total number of questions — 20
63
Adverse effects of present
examination system
†*181. SHRI SHIVANAND
TIWARI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a study has
been conducted on adverse effects on
students due to pressure of examination
under the present education system;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard and the
ill-effects observed due to pressure and
stress of the current examination system;
(c) whether Government has taken any
decision to make changes in the present
examination system; and
(d) if so, the details of the decisions
taken in this regard?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Pending cases in subordinate
courts
*182. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL
DARDA:
 Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
more than three crore cases are pending in
various subordinate courts across the country;
(b) if so, the facts and details
thereof;
(c) whether the factors responsible for
such pendency in subordinate courts have
ever been assessed;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the steps taken/directions issued by
Government to speed up disposal of cases
in subordinate courts?

64
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Laws on live-in relationship
†*183. SHRI PRABHA T JHA: Will the
Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some States
have passed laws relating to live-in
relationship and sent the same to the Central
Government for approval;
(b) if so, Government's views in this
regard;
(c) whether Government would
consider rejecting such laws, keeping in
view the Indian society and culture;
(d) if so, details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
India's ranking in UNESCO report
*184. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that UNESCO's
Global Monitoring report places India in
the bottom of 15 countries, with a low
‘Education for All’ development index, and
India's ranking in the fight against illiteracy
has slipped from 100 last year to 105 now;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government has pumped more funds into
education without corresponding outcome;
and
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government
to improve the situation?
Environmental impact assessment of
hydro power projects
*185. SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD
BAISHYA: Will the Minister of POWER
be pleased to state:
(a) the details of environment impact
assessment made, specially towards the
effect of flood and erosion, including
siltation on the downstream of existing as
well as to be executed hydro power projects
in Arunachal Pradesh and neighbouring
countires like Bhutan and Nepal, project-
wise; and
(b) the details of power shared within
the North-Eastern States from the existing
power projects as well as projects to be set
up in North-Eastern Region (NER),
Project-wise?
Legislative proposals on child sexual
abuse
*186. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether her Ministry has any
specific proposals on legislation and
procedures against child sexual abuse; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Zonal benches of Supreme Court
*187. DR. JANARDHAN
WAGHMARE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Chief justice of India has
used Government to set up zonal benches
of the Supreme Court and allow the principal
bench to hear cases only on constitutional
matters and inter-state disputes;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government proposes to
set up zonal benches of Supreme Court in
various parts of the country; and

65
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Augmentation of transmission
capacity
†*188. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI :
Will the Minister of  POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as against
the current capacity, a target of threefold
increase in the power transmission capacity
in the country by 2012 has been set;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard;
(c) whether it is also a fact that very
limited transformer testing facility is
available in the country;
(d) if so, whether 90 MV A capacity
transformers are sent abroad for testing;
and
(e) if so, the details in this regard and
the reasons for not establishing the said
testing facility in the country?
Retirement age of teachers
*189. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is considering
any proposal to increase the retirement age
of teachers of NCERT to 65 years;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Prof. Chadha Committee
has also recommended to increase the
retirement age of teachers, including NCERT
teachers to 65 years, in view of shortage of
teachers;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) what is the reaction of Government
to it?
Social audit of RGGVY
*190. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the Minister of POWER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has recently
decided to have social audit of the Rajiv
Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana
(RGGVY) and to ensure transparency in
implementation of the scheme;
(b) if so, the facts and details thereof;
(c) whether several States in the country
are lagging behind in implementing the
scheme; and
(d) if so, the facts thereof and the steps
taken to implement the scheme in an
effective way?
Pending court cases
*191. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
 Will the Minister of LAW AND
JUSTICE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether a large number of cases are
pending with various High Courts and the
Supreme Court;
(b) if so, whether Government's decision
to increase the working hours would help
in reducing the huge backlog of court cases;
(c) whether experts have suggested that
the immediate need is to change the mindset
and the work culture;

66
(d) if so, what are the views expressed
by experts in reducing the backlog of court
cases; and
(e) the steps being considered by the
Central Government in this regard?
Non-availability of basic facilities in
rural schools
*192. SHRIMA TI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Government has
expressed its serious concern over the non-
availability of toilets and potable water in
all the rural schools in the country;
(b) whether Government has decided
that it is compulsory that teachers, toilets,
potable water and other necessary facilities
are made available to all the rural schools in
the country;
(c)  if so, what is the percentage of
schools, at present, where there are no such
facilities; and
(d) whether Government has made it
compulsory that all the schools, especially
in rural areas, should have such facilities
before starting operation of schools?
Return on investments made in SEBs
*193. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of POWER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has envisaged
certain minimum Return on Investments
(RoI) made in each of the State Electricity
Boards (SEBs);
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of total funds lying
invested in SEBs, State-wise, till
30th September, 2008, indicating the annual
rate of gross and net returns achieved by
each, year-wise, since 2000-01;
(d) the steps initiated, if any, in respect
of SEBs where RoI remained below the
minimum level and/or suffered negative
RoI;
(e) whether Government has conducted
any study into the affairs of such SEBs;
(f) if so, the outcome of the exercise;
and
(g) if not, the reasons therefor?
Hydel power generation
*194. DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government is giving top
priority to exploit hydel potential in India,
as hydel power is cheaper than the nuclear
energy;
(b) whether Government proposes to
implement a 40 MW hydro electric project
on river Beas;
(c) whether Government has decided to
give priority to power sector during the
Eleventh Five Year Plan;
(d) if so, what concrete measures and
steps Government is considering to take to
improve the hydel power projects; and
(e) by when all the power projects, that
are being presently set up, would be
completed and what would be the total
power generation (in MWs) after
completion of these projects?
Meetings of Tribal Advisory Bodies or
Committees
*195. SHRIMATI T. RATNA BAI:
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:

67
(a) whether Government is regularly
convening the meetings of Tribal Advisory
Bodies or Committees;
(b) if so, the details threof;
(c) what is the time-frame for convening
such meetings; and
(d) what are the guidelines issued in this
regard?
Allocation of power from Mega Power
Projects
*196. SHRI P .R. RAJAN:
SHRI A. VIJAYA-
RAGHA VAN:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government had placed the
condition of privatization of distribution,
for allocation of power from Mega Power
Projects;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Kerala Government had
represented, during 2007-08, for removal
of the above condition under peculiar
circumstances of the State;
(d) if so, the action taken thereon;
(e) whether a decision would be taken
in affirmative to the above representation;
and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Setting up of Central Universities
*197. SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL
DARDA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
set up 12 more Central Universities, adding
to its present strength;
(b) whether the budget allocation for
opening of these universities was Rs. 3,280
crore;
(c) if so, what are total universities at
present in the country;
(d) to what extent creation of 12 more
universities would help in improving the
education in the country;
(e) whether there are still many States
where these universities are not set up; and
(f) if so, by when these universities
would start functioning?
Provincialisation of schools in Assam
*198. KUMAR DEEPAK DAS: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether a large number of Lower
Primary, Middle English, High School and
Higher Secondary schools have been set
up in Assam with due permission of the
Union Government, during the last many
years and if so, the details thereof
year-wise and district-wise;
(b) whether it is a fact that Government
has failed to provincialise the services of
the teachers and the school buildings are
also in a very deplorable condition; and
(c) whether the Ministry would adopt
any policy for solution of such problems
and if so, the details thereof?
Reservation for disabled persons in
private sector
†*199. SHRI AJAY SINGH
CHAUTALA: W ill the Minister of
SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

68
NEW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 8th December, 2008 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 17, 1930 (Saka)
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has failed in providing concessions and
encouragement to the disabled persons in
the country;
(b) whether Government proposes to
make a legislation whereby the disabled
persons could get reservation in private
companies and could contribute in nation's
development; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and, if not,
the reasons therefor?
Health hazards in asbestos mining
†*200. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI KRISHAN LAL
BALMIKI:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Indian
Bureau of Mines has conducted a study on
the effect on the health of labourers engaged
in asbestos mining;
(b) if so, whether this study has made
any suggestions;
(c) whether the study group has
suggested doing away with the restrictions
on asbestos mining;
(d) whether Government proposes to
implement them;
(e) whether Government would lift the
ban on new leases for asbestos mining and
their renewal; and
(f) if so, by when?
